LESSON: SIGN READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: NARRATIVES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Sign Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Narratives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Narratives, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read narratives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words and phrases related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Narratives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. sign read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Narratives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply appropriate sign reading strategies to sign read a narrative of about 320 words for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Narratives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate sign reading for purposes of comprehension and information. ● In pairs, learners are guided to watch a captioned video clip or observe a signed demonstration of vocabulary related to Hiv and Aids. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to Hiv and Aids. ● In groups, learners are guided to sign read vocabulary items from a short narrative. ● In pairs, learners are guided to skim through a narrative. ● In pairs, learners are guided to scan a narrative to obtain specific information. ● In pairs, learners are guided to sign read a passage in print or non-print format and answer questions. ● In groups, learners are guided to, through signs, discuss vocabulary from the passage and use them to construct simple sentences. ● In groups, learners are guided to answer factual and inferential questions from a passage. ● In groups, learners are guided to tell and sign stories related to the theme. ● In groups, learners are guided to give the sequence of events in a given story or passage. ● In groups, learners are guided to, through signs, discuss and role play events in a passage. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Narratives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner develops the skill of teamwork as they retell stories related to the theme in pairs and groups.

● Self- efficacy: learner develop efficacy as they answer inferential and factual questions correctly.

Values:
Unity: inclusion as learners sign read a digital text online or offline and answer question in groups or pairs.

Link to other subjects
